scope: Corollary 8.1 (Bounded integral flows) of the manuscript “An FPRAS for Cell-Bounded Contingency Tables” (preprints/An-FPRAS-for-Cell-Bounded-Contingency-Tables-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 115 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 10bad4277d11b9d1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the network data above, there are algorithms with these guarantees. (i) Given rational ε, δ ∈ (0, 1), the counting algorithm outputs a nonnegative rational b Zflow satisfying P (1 − ε)|F| ≤ b Zflow ≤ (1 + ε)|F|  ≥ 1 − δ. If F is empty, it outputs zero on every execution. (ii) Given rational τ ∈ (0, 1), the sampling algorithm reports infeasibility exactly when F is empty. Otherwise it outputs b f ∈ F on every execution, with TV L( b f), Unif(F)  = 1 2 X f∈F P( b f = f) − 1 |F| ≤ τ. Both algorithms use independent unbiased bits. Let L denote the total binary input length, including the corresponding accuracy parameters. Fixed polynomials in L, ε−1, log(δ−1) for counting and in L, τ−1 for sampling bound the total bit operations on every execution.
